## Indexing and data transformations

```{r}
set.seed(123)
age <- sample(1:90, size = 10, replace = TRUE)
age[age == 14]
age[age > 60 | age <18]
age[age == 18 | age >18 & age <65 | age == 65]
age[age >= 18 & age <= 65]

##Altermative
idx <- age > 60| age <18
age[idx]

##To check the presence of one vector in another
A <- seq(1, 12, 2)  # odd numbers
B <- seq(2, 12, 2)  # even numbers

# test to see if each of the elements of A is in B  
A %in% B

## Another example
epi <- str_split_1("epidemiology", "")
epi
epi <- str_split_1("epidemiology", "")
epi
epi[are_vowels]
```

```{r}
## Useful fucntions on vectors
##sort and order
v <- runif(5, min=1, max=10)
sort(v)
order(v)
```

```{r}
w <- c(6.1, 8.9, NA, 5.0, 8.8, 1.9, 6.6, 7.2, 9.4, NA, 4.9)

mean(w)
mean(w, na.rm = TRUE)
```

score

## From Vectors to matrices

```{r}
# `matrix()` defines a matrix with 3 rows and 4 columns
A <- matrix(1:12, nrow = 3, ncol = 4) 
A

# same result is obtained by providing only one dimension
matrix(sample(0:5, 12, replace = TRUE), nrow = 3)

# same result is obtained by providing only one dimension
matrix(1:12, nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)
```

```{r}
## Exercise
m<- matrix(1:6, nrow = 2)
m
matrix(1:6, nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
matrix(0, nrow=3, ncol=3)

zero <- rep(0,9)
m <- matrix(zero, ncol=3)
```

```{r}
##Accessing elements of a matrix
A <- matrix(1:12, nrow = 3, ncol = 4) 
A[c(1, 2), c(2, 3)]
##leaving column field blank will select entire columns
A[c(1, 2), ]
#Select all the rows except first
A[-1, ]

##Logical vectors can be used to index a matrix rows and columns where the value is TRUE is returned...

##Logical vectors can be used to index a matrix rows and columns where the value is TRUE is returned

A <- matrix(c(4, 9, 10, 1, 5, 7), nrow = 3)
A
dim(A)
A(2,2) 
A <- cbind(0,0,0)
A [1,1] <- 0
A
t(A)
```

```{r}
temperature_class <- factor(rep(c("cold", "warm", "mild"), each=3))
temperature_class
as.integer(temperature_class)
set.seed(3)
temperatures <- rnorm(12,10,10)
temperatures

w_class <- c(-15, 0, 15, 30)
cut(temperatures, breaks = w_class,
    labels = levels(temperature_class))
```
